Verdict: request experiment.

Does not favour top over runner-up: atlas is 4-4 (DNA replication mean sim 0.649 vs kinase 0.641; top-hit margin only 0.034), phenotype is explicitly 'unknown' with intact microtubules/actin, and DNA-dimming/hypertrophy/loss of mitotics are compatible with DNA-replication arrest too. Compound: **methotrexate** (PubChem CID [126941](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/126941))

ChEMBL mechanisms: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor

## Reflection

The strongest signal was extreme loss of nuclear DNA intensity with cell hypertrophy: nuc_dna_mean z=-11.9 at 0.3 uM and z=-10.1 at 10 uM with cell_area z=+7.1 to +7.7, lower density and loss of mitotics. The reference atlas consistently kept DNA replication in the top two at 4/10 then 4/10 and 3/10, which correctly kept the antimetabolite DNA-replication class alive and ultimately matched methotrexate dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor annotation.

What misled the first call was saturation and a tie broken badly. Both acquired wells were single-replicate and already maximal, so all dose-response checks failed for lack of a third well, and the per-well atlas split with only a 0.034 top-hit margin between DNA replication mean sim 0.649 and kinase 0.641. I over-weighted intact microtubules/actin plus hypertrophy as G1-like kinase arrest and called kinase inhibitors at p=0.36 over DNA replication at 0.30 despite the microscopist reporting unknown.

The review critique was correct to demand a sub-saturating 0.03 uM well to resolve partial effects, and the revised low-confidence DNA replication call at p=0.32 vs 0.30 was appropriate for an unresolved tie. The lesson is not to break atlas ties on top-hit margin when DNA dimming, low density and loss of mitotics fit S-phase block equally well and saturation prevents a trend.

What was right:
- Extreme nuc_dna_mean loss with increased cell_area and nuc_solidity flagged DNA-synthesis block and cell-cycle arrest rather than cytoskeletal or mitotic toxicity
- Reference atlas repeatedly ranked DNA replication 4/10 alongside kinase inhibitors, keeping the true antimetabolite class in contention
- Revised DNA replication call at p=0.32 acknowledged the kinase tie and matched unblinded methotrexate dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor mechanism

What was wrong or missed:
- First kinase inhibitors conclusion at p=0.36 overstated separation from DNA replication at 0.30 by breaking a 4-4 atlas tie on a 0.034 similarity margin
- Acquired only high 10 uM and mid 0.3 uM single-replicate saturated wells, so dose_response for nuc_dna_mean, cell_area, cell_count and frac_mitotic_like all failed and masked discriminative partial effects
- Over-interpreted hypertrophy with intact microtubules/actin and explicitly unknown microscopist phenotype as G1 kinase arrest while under-weighting that DNA dimming plus lower density fits S-phase replication arrest

Proposed next experiment: EdU pulse plus PI flow cytometry across a sub-saturating methotrexate dilution series including 0.03 uM, with thymidine/folinic acid rescue and a cell-free DHFR activity assay to test S-phase DNA-synthesis block versus kinase-mediated G1 arrest.
